cards.b: A push or a pull, measured in newtons (N).

cards.f: Effect of more force on the same mass
cards.b: Greater acceleration (or deceleration if the force opposes the motion).
Gravity, air resistance and muscular force.

cards.f: Forces on a sprinter in the blocks
cards.b: Gravity, ground reaction force and air resistance.

cards.f: Forces on an object flying through the air
cards.b: Force applied at release, air resistance and gravity.
The ground pushes back on the performer with an equal and opposite force when they push on it.
A force opposing the motion of a performer or object through the air; reduced by streamlining.
A rigid bar (bone) that pivots around a fulcrum (joint) when effort is applied.
The pivot point of a lever; in the body, the joint.
Effort is the force applied by the muscle; resistance (load) is the weight or force being moved.
Fulcrum in the middle (E-F-R). Example: neck nodding.
Resistance in the middle (F-R-E). Example: ankle when rising on to the toes.
Effort in the middle (F-E-R). Example: elbow in a bicep curl; the most common type.
1-2-3 = F-R-E: the item in the middle is fulcrum, resistance, effort.

gaps.s: The pivot point of a lever is called the ___.
The bicep curl is an example of a ___-class lever.
The force the ground exerts back on a sprinter's feet is the ground ___ force.
In a second-class lever the ___ is in the middle.
After a javelin is released, the force that pulls it to the ground is ___.
A 20 kg object accelerating at 3 m/s² needs a force of ___ N.

short.q: A 65 kg player accelerates at 3 m/s². Calculate the force.
Name three forces acting on a cyclist.
short.model: Gravity, air resistance and muscular force (pushing the pedals).

short.q: Identify the fulcrum, effort and resistance in a bicep curl.
short.model: Fulcrum is the elbow joint, effort is the biceps muscle, resistance is the weight of the forearm and dumbbell.
points: Effort: biceps; resistance: weight in hand

short.q: Explain why a shot put follows a curved path after release.
short.model: After release the only forces acting are gravity pulling it down and air resistance slowing it, so it follows a curved path to the ground.
points: No force from the thrower after release

short.q: State the class of lever at the ankle when rising onto tiptoes and give the order of its parts.
short.model: It is a second-class lever: fulcrum (ball of foot), resistance (body weight at the ankle), effort (calf muscle at the heel).
